the identification of genomic and transcriptomic alterations in cancer, their associations with DNA mutational signatures, and their associations with clinical features.
the genomic basis of RNA alterations in cancer and we present, to the best of our knowledge, the largest and most comprehensive catalogue of RNA alterations in cancers to date.

The main takeaway from our work is that

somatic copy number alterations are the major drivers of total gene and allele-specific expression, whereas the remaining RNA alterations are associated with somatic DNA alterations and have a wide range of underlying genetic mechanisms, including splicing, fusion and non coding RNA changes.
